rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebuts idolaters: why worship what cannot benefit or harm, then return to shirk after God rescued and guided us?
rows.anchor: أي أنعبد من دون الله النافع الضار ما لا يقدر على نفعنا ولا على ضرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning from truth to falsehood is called going back on one's heels because people begin ignorant, gain knowledge, and then regress to their original ignorance.
rows.anchor: فإذا رجع من العلم إلى الجهل مرة أخرى فكأنه رجع إلى أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads the verb in masculine form with an imāla alif; the other readers use the feminine because a plural can be treated as a collective group.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة { * استهواه } بألف ممالة على التذكير والباقون بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred derivation takes the verb from physical descent into a deep hollow; the falling person's agitation and weakness sharpen the image of the lost person.
rows.anchor: أنه مشتق من الهوى في الأرض ، وهو النزول من الموضع العالي إلى الوهدة السافلة العميقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second derivation connects the verb with following desire and inclination, which can lead to extreme bewilderment; Razi prefers physical descent as the fuller image.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أنه مشتق من اتباع الهوى والميل

rows.speaker: الأصمعي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī gives ḥāra, ḥīra, and ḥayr; al-Farrāʾ adds ḥayrān and ḥayrūra, all describing hesitation without finding a way out.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي : يقال حار يحار حيرة وحيرا ، وزاد الفراء حيرانا وحيرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the parable exceptionally apt: a person falling from a height tumbles, cannot know where he will land, and fears whether the landing will worsen his plight.
rows.anchor: علمت أنك لا تجد مثالا للمتحير المتردد الخائف أحسن ولا أكمل من هذا المثال

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes report that the verse was revealed about ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr, who called his father to disbelief while his father called him to faith; Razi says this is correct.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه فإنه كان يدعو أباه إلى الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A different interpretation says the lost unbeliever's companions invite him toward their own misguidance while calling it guidance; Razi considers this remote.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد أن لذلك الكافر الضال أصحابا يدعونه إلى ذلك الضلال ويسمونه بأنه هو الهدى وهذا بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God's guidance the guidance means it is guidance perfected in completeness, benefit, and honor, as in calling someone's knowledge or kingship the true thing of its kind.
rows.anchor: يعني هو الهدى الكامل النافع الشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guidance encompasses every command and avoidance of every prohibition, including heart and bodily actions as well as abstention from what is improper.
rows.anchor: دخل فيه جميع أقسام المأمورات والاحتراز عن كل المنهيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the general statement about guidance, the passage names Islam as the leading spiritual obedience, prayer as the leading bodily obedience, and taqwā as the leading restraint.
rows.anchor: أشرف أقسامه على الترتيب وهو الإسلام الذي هو رئيس الطاعات الروحانية ، والصلاة التي هي رئيسة الطاعات الجسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The benefit of these acts becomes manifest on the day of gathering, resurrection, and judgment.
rows.anchor: إنما تظهر في يوم الحشر والبعث والقيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's debate is an argument against Arab polytheists because all religious communities honored him, and the polytheists acknowledged both his merit and their descent from him.
rows.anchor: المشركون كانوا معترفين بفضله مقرين بأنهم من أولاده واليهود والنصارى والمسلمون كلهم معظمون له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's unique standing followed a covenant: he fulfilled servanthood, as God attests both generally and specifically in the trials and command to submit.
rows.anchor: فإبراهيم وفى بعهد العبودية ، والله تعالى شهد بذلك على سبيل الإجمال تارة وعلى سبيل التفصيل أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham demonstrated monotheism in debates with his father, his people, and the ruler, by smashing idols, enduring the threat of burning, and offering his son.
rows.anchor: ناظر في إثبات التوحيد وإبطال القول بالشركاء والأنداد في مقامات كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gave his heart to knowledge, tongue to proof, body to fire, child to sacrifice, and wealth to guests; God answered his prayer for lasting good mention, making him honored among all communities.
rows.anchor: سلم قلبه للعرفان ولسانه للبرهان وبدنه للنيران وولده للقربان وماله للضيفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Arabs acknowledged Abraham's merit, God made his debate with his people a proof against Arab polytheists.
rows.anchor: ولما كان العرب معترفين بفضله لا جرم جعل الله تعالى مناظرته مع قومه حجة على مشركي العرب

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the clause about night covering Abraham coordinates with Abraham's speech to his father, while “Thus We showed” is an intervening parenthesis.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { فلما جن عليه اليل } عطف على قوله : { قال إبراهيم لابيه ءازر }

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the preferred idioms are “night covered him” and “night came over him”; janna means concealment and underlies the listed words for garden, jinn, madness, embryo, and grave.
rows.anchor: هذا قول جميع أهل اللغة ، ومعنى { جن } ستر ومنه الجنة والجن والجنون

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians take janna ʿalayhi al-layl to mean that night darkened over him, which accounts for ʿalā; jannahū means simply covered him without the sense of darkness.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين : { جن عليه اليل } إذا أظلم عليه الليل

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes recount that a king, warned a boy would contest his rule, ordered newborn boys killed; Abraham was hidden in a cave, miraculously sustained by Gabriel, and later sought his Lord after his mother and father answered that they served as his lords and the king ruled them.
rows.anchor: فأمر ذلك الملك بذبح كل غلام يولد ، فحبلت أم إبراهيم به وماأظهرت حبلها للناس

rows.speaker: أكثر المحققين
rows.claim: Most rigorous scholars reject the view that Abraham's stargazing occurred after puberty and the onset of legal responsibility; they argue against it in the following discussion.
rows.anchor: واتفق أكثر المحققين على فساد القول الأول واحتجوا عليه بوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Argument one: affirming a star as Lord is unanimously disbelief, and disbelief is unanimously impossible for prophets.
rows.anchor: أن القول بربوبية النجم كفر بالإجماع والكفر غير جائز بالإجماع على الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Argument two: Abraham already knew his Lord, since he had confronted his father Āzar about taking idols as gods before this episode.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى أخبر عنه أنه قال قبل هذه الواقعة لأبيه آزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Argument three: Abraham first used gentle speech with his father; a preacher resorts to harshness only after sustained gentle appeals and despair, so the episode came after he knew God and had repeatedly called his father.
rows.anchor: من دعا غيره إلى الله تعالى فإنه يقدم الرفق على العنف واللين على الغلظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Argument four: after God showed Abraham the kingdom of heaven and earth, it is inconceivable that he would regard celestial bodies as divine.
rows.anchor: ومن كان منصبه في الدين كذلك ، وعلمه بالله كذلك ، كيف يليق به أن يعتقد إلهية الكواكب ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Argument five: the heavens display at least fifteen signs of origination, making star-worship implausible even for a person of little reason, let alone Abraham.
rows.anchor: دلائل الحدوث في الأفلاك ظاهرة من خمسة عشر وجها وأكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Argument six: God calls Abraham pure of heart, which at minimum means free from disbelief, and says he received sound guidance from early in his reflection; God knows where to place His message.
rows.anchor: إذ جاء ربه بقلب سليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Argument seven: the narrative's sequence places the stargazing after God showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and earth and made him certain in faith.
rows.anchor: والفاء تقتضي الترتيب ، فثبت أن هذه الواقعة إنما وقعت بعد أن صار إبراهيم من الموقنين العارفين بربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Argument eight: the passage identifies the debate as proof against Abraham's people, showing that he argued to guide them rather than seek knowledge for himself.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل على نفسه ، فعلم أن هذه المباحثة إنما جرت مع قومه لأجل أن يرشدهم إلى الإيمان والتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Argument twelve: if Abraham sought knowledge for himself, the sun's setting the previous day should already have disproved its divinity, and therefore the moon's and star's a fortiori; in a public debate, the dialogue could instead begin at the star's rising and continue through the moon and sun.
rows.anchor: كان ينبغي أن يستدل بغروبها السابق على أنها لا تصلح للآلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These arguments rule out Abraham's making a definite assertion that a star was his Lord; Razi then leaves two possible explanations of the words.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يجوز أن يقال إن إبراهيم عليه السلام قال على سبيل الجزم : هذا ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First explanation, which Razi calls the relied-upon answer: Abraham repeats the star-worshippers' claim so he can refute it, just as a debater restates an opponent's premise before exposing its contradiction.
rows.anchor: بل الغرض منه أنه كان يناظر عبدة الكوكب وكان مذهبهم أن الكوكب ربهم وآلههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation means “this is my Lord” according to the opponents' belief, as in scriptural language that speaks from the addressees' own perspective.
rows.anchor: معناه هذا ربي في زعمكم واعتقادكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation treats the words as a rhetorical question of denial, with the interrogative particle omitted because the context makes it clear.
rows.anchor: المراد منه الاستفهام على سبيل الإنكار إلا أنه أسقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth explanation supplies an omitted “they say”: Abraham tells his people that they claim this is the one who manages and raises him, as in other verses with implicit speech.
rows.anchor: والتقدير : قال يقولون هذا ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth explanation reads the statement as mockery, like sarcastically calling a lowly person who has become leader “your master.”
rows.anchor: أن يكون إبراهيم ذكر هذا الكلام على سبيل الاستهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth explanation says Abraham outwardly seemed to agree with the star-worshippers to draw an entrenched audience into hearing the proof, while his heart remained faithful; the apparent concession is justified by the benefit of guiding them.
rows.anchor: ذكر كلاما يوهم كونه مساعدا لهم على مذهبهم بربوبية الكواكب مع أن قلبه صلوات الله عليه كان مطمئنا بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that urgent rescue can take priority over prayer, and that apparent conformity to the audience can likewise serve the greater duty of saving a community from disbelief.
rows.anchor: وجب عليه قطع الصلاة لإنقاذ ذلك الطفل أو ذلك الأعمى عن ذلك البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's earlier claim to be sick similarly appeared to follow astrologers' assumptions, while his actual aim was to leave and break the idols; this supports strategic outward accommodation.
rows.anchor: ومقصوده أن يتوسل بهذا الطريق إلى كسر الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theologians permit apparent wonders from someone claiming divinity because the claim is obviously false, while prophetic pretensions could mislead; likewise the star statement's clear counter-evidence prevents misguidance and lets Abraham lead people to proof.
rows.anchor: لا يوجب الضلال ، لأن دلائل بطلانه جلية وفي إظهاره هذه الكلمة منفعة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seventh post-puberty explanation says Abraham echoed the star that the people invited him to worship, waited until it set, and then rejected it as one that sets.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الرب الذي تدعونني إليه ثم سكت زمانا حتى أفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second overall possibility places the inquiry before puberty: Abraham's perfect intellect led him to test the Creator through the star, reject it when it set, and reach puberty during the inquiry, when he declared himself free of shirk.
rows.anchor: خطر بباله قبل بلوغه إثبات الصانع سبحانه فتفكر فرأى النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi accepts the pre-puberty possibility but prefers a post-puberty debate intended to call the people to monotheism, in light of the many arguments given earlier.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الاحتمال الأول أولى بالقبول لما ذكرنا من الدلائل الكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers vary the vocalization of raʾā: Abū ʿAmr and Warsh open rāʾ and kasra hamza; Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī have paired kasras, with further differences before k/h and hamzat al-waṣl; al-Wāḥidī explains them by retaining the original, imāla, or matching vowels.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وورش عن نافع { * رئى } بفتح الراء وكسر الهمزة حيث كان
